metadata.case_name: CHU MAN TING v. KWAN KAM KEI AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: She sustained a depressed skull fracture which caused swelling of the brain.
source: She sustained a depressed skull fracture which caused swelling of the brain.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of vault of skull, unspecified

injuries.description: The CT scan of the brain showed diffuse cerebral oedema with traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage.
source: The CT scan of the brain showed diffuse cerebral oedema with traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage.

injuries.description: A scan of the cervical spine revealed a crack fracture of C3 and C4 of the vertebral body.
source: A scan of the cervical spine revealed a crack fracture of C3 and C4 of the vertebral body.

injuries.description: There was left sided haemothorax (a collection of blood in the chest cavity).
source: There was left sided haemothorax (a collection of blood in the chest cavity).

injuries.description: X-ray examination showed a fractured left clavicle,
source: X-ray examination showed a fractured left clavicle,

injuries.description: a comminuted fracture of the right forearm (distal radius and ulna)
source: a comminuted fracture of the right forearm (distal radius and ulna)
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of lower end of both ulna and radius

injuries.description: a fracture of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd metacarpals of the right hand.
source: a fracture of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd metacarpals of the right hand.

manifestations.description: Loss of consciousness / comatose for a number of days
Glasgow Coma Scale was 7/15 on arrival
Headaches associated with dizziness, such headaches occurring daily and lasting from one to two hours which had been brought on by mental tasks
Dizziness occurring daily and could last for up to three or four hours
Short term memory was poor; recent memory continues to remain impaired; difficulty retaining study material
Poor sense of direction; needed to be accompanied by an adult when visiting unfamiliar places
Change in personality: developed a capacity for irritability and lack of inhibition (for example, singing during class); reduced social functioning and poor personal relations with fellow pupils
Over-eating causing obesity; weight having risen at one stage to 93.6 kg
Dizziness contributed to two separate falls which caused fractures
Increased risk of post-traumatic epilepsy compared to normal population

source: she was intubated and supported with mechanical ventilation.

treatments_received.treatment: Managed in the Intensive Care Unit for about two weeks
source: She was managed by the Intensive Care Unit for about two weeks following the accident

treatments_received.treatment: Operation to repair fractured forearm (performed on 9 April 1999)
source: an operation was performed on 9 April 1999 some 11 days after the accident, delayed presumably in order to allow time for her condition to stabilize.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Open reduction for arm / leg / patella / scapula +/- internal fixation

treatments_received.treatment: Removal of implants (re-admitted 6 to 10 July 2000 for removal of implants inserted in the operation to repair her fractured forearm)
source: She was then re-admitted for four days, from 6 to 10 July 2000, for the removal of implants which had been inserted in the operation to repair her fractured forearm.
having been given physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and counselling.
having been given physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and counselling.
having been given physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and counselling.
having been given physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and counselling.
The intracranial pressure was monitored and albeit slowly, she improved.

treatments_future.treatment: Psychological counselling for plaintiff: biweekly for one year (26 sessions) and monthly for a further year (12 sessions)
source: For Man Ting, I allow biweekly sessions (by which I understood the Professor to mean once every two weeks) for the first year which would be 26 sessions multiplied by $1,500, being $39,000 and for the second year, 12 multiplied by $1,500, making $18,000.

treatments_future.treatment: Psychological counselling for parents: eight separate sessions
source: For the parents, I will make an allowance for eight separate sessions for them, making 8 multiplied by $1,500, being $12,000.

losses.description: Diminution in her overall intellectual capacities; measured reduction of IQ; poor recent memory and reduced ability to retain study material.

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: She was obliged to repeat Form 1 and Form 2, is two years behind her chronological age and faces a real risk of perhaps not getting into university.
Change in personality with increased irritability and lack of inhibition; socially inappropriate behaviour and reduced social functioning.
Poor personal relations with fellow pupils at school; victim of unkind bullying and loss of good friends.
Difficulties at home and not getting on well with her parents following the accident.
